refuted at smallest parameters: r=2, k=2 family I₁={2,3}, I₂={24,25} gives total product 3600=60², exactly verified; Pell a(a+1)=6t² yields infinitely many length-2 square-product blocks, so k=2 imposes no obstruction and any close must use a fixed r across all k≥2 with explicit integrality.

REFUTED by external audit (GPT gold-mine audit + R4, 2026-09-01), each item re-verified by the operator's session against the frozen contract or by exact computation on 2026-09-02 | FALSE: Pintz/Rankin-type results concern LARGE GAPS between consecutive primes, not the length of arithmetic progressions of primes in [1,N]. No theorem gives L(N) = omega(log N) infinitely often; the longest known prime APs in [1,N] have length far below log N and the o(log N) question is open. 'negative close achieved' is a citation misuse.

exact W16.1 enumeration of all 4 triples at N=4 certifies TWO sum-distinct n=3 extremizers {(1,2,4),(2,3,4)} (witness (1,2,4): sums 0..7 distinct); uniqueness of {2,3,4} is refuted; corrected claim: N(3)=4 with exactly two extremizers; scope = complete finite domain, no analytic remainder.

All-primes choice makes the a_k sequence finite, violating the canonical premise; vacuous-goodness argument is domain drift, needs an infinite survivor construction plus literal quantifier-order verification.
